> **Difficulty:** Easy | **Acceptance:** 61.10% | **Paid:** No
> **Topics:** Math

Return the number of permutations of 1 to n so that prime numbers are at prime indices (1-indexed).

Since the answer may be large, return the answer modulo 10⁹ + 7.

- Examples
- Constraints
- [Sieve of Eratosthenes](#sieve-of-eratosthenes)
- [Iterative Primality Test](#iterative-primality-test)
- [Precomputation](#precomputation)

## Examples

### Example 1
```text
Input: n = 5
Output: 12
Explanation: [1,2,5,3,4] is one valid permutation. 
[1,4,5,2,3] is also a valid permutation.
```

### Example 2
```text
Input: n = 1
Output: 1
```

## Constraints

```text
1 <= n <= 100
```

---
## Sieve of Eratosthenes

**Intuition**
We need to count how many prime numbers exist between 1 and n. Let this count be k. We have k prime numbers and k prime indices. The number of ways to arrange k items in k positions is k!. Similarly, we have n - k non-prime numbers and n - k non-prime indices, which can be arranged in (n - k)! ways. The total valid permutations are the product of these two factorials.

**Steps**
- Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to identify all prime numbers up to n.
- Count the total number of primes, k.
- Calculate the factorial of k modulo 10⁹ + 7.
- Calculate the factorial of (n - k) modulo 10⁹ + 7.
- Multiply the two results and return the product modulo 10⁹ + 7.

<CodeTabs client:load tabs={[{ name: "Python3", lang: "python", code: "class Solution:\n    def numPrimeArrangements(self, n: int) -&gt; int:\n        MOD = 10**9 + 7\n        \n        # Sieve of Eratosthenes\n        is_prime = [True] * (n + 1)\n        if n &gt;= 0:\n            is_prime[0] = False\n        if n &gt;= 1:\n            is_prime[1] = False\n            \n        for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):\n            if is_prime[i]:\n                for j in range(i * i, n + 1, i):\n                    is_prime[j] = False\n                    \n        k = sum(is_prime)\n        \n        # Calculate k! * (n-k)! % MOD\n        res = 1\n        for i in range(1, k + 1):\n            res = (res * i) % MOD\n            \n        for i in range(1, n - k + 1):\n            res = (res * i) % MOD\n            \n        return res" },
{ name: "Java", lang: "java", code: "class Solution {\n    public int numPrimeArrangements(int n) {\n        int MOD = 1000000007;\n        \n        // Sieve of Eratosthenes\n        boolean[] isPrime = new boolean[n + 1];\n        Arrays.fill(isPrime, true);\n        if (n &gt;= 0) isPrime[0] = false;\n        if (n &gt;= 1) isPrime[1] = false;\n        \n        for (int i = 2; i * i &lt;= n; i++) {\n            if (isPrime[i]) {\n                for (int j = i * i; j &lt;= n; j += i) {\n                    isPrime[j] = false;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        \n        int k = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n            if (isPrime[i]) k++;\n        }\n        \n        // Calculate k! * (n-k)! % MOD\n        long res = 1;\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        \n        return (int) res;\n    }\n}" },
{ name: "C++", lang: "cpp", code: "class Solution {\npublic:\n    int numPrimeArrangements(int n) {\n        const int MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n        \n        // Sieve of Eratosthenes\n        vector&lt;bool&gt; isPrime(n + 1, true);\n        if (n &gt;= 0) isPrime[0] = false;\n        if (n &gt;= 1) isPrime[1] = false;\n        \n        for (int i = 2; i * i &lt;= n; ++i) {\n            if (isPrime[i]) {\n                for (int j = i * i; j &lt;= n; j += i) {\n                    isPrime[j] = false;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        \n        int k = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i &lt;= n; ++i) {\n            if (isPrime[i]) ++k;\n        }\n        \n        // Calculate k! * (n-k)! % MOD\n        long long res = 1;\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= k; ++i) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; ++i) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        \n        return (int)res;\n    }\n};" },
{ name: "JavaScript", lang: "javascript", code: "var numPrimeArrangements = function(n) {\n    const MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n    \n    // Sieve of Eratosthenes\n    const isPrime = new Array(n + 1).fill(true);\n    if (n &gt;= 0) isPrime[0] = false;\n    if (n &gt;= 1) isPrime[1] = false;\n    \n    for (let i = 2; i * i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime[i]) {\n            for (let j = i * i; j &lt;= n; j += i) {\n                isPrime[j] = false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    let k = 0;\n    for (let i = 0; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime[i]) k++;\n    }\n    \n    // Calculate k! * (n-k)! % MOD\n    let res = 1n;\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    \n    return Number(res);\n};" },
{ name: "TypeScript", lang: "typescript", code: "function numPrimeArrangements(n: number): number {\n    const MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n    \n    // Sieve of Eratosthenes\n    const isPrime: boolean[] = new Array(n + 1).fill(true);\n    if (n &gt;= 0) isPrime[0] = false;\n    if (n &gt;= 1) isPrime[1] = false;\n    \n    for (let i = 2; i * i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime[i]) {\n            for (let j = i * i; j &lt;= n; j += i) {\n                isPrime[j] = false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    let k = 0;\n    for (let i = 0; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime[i]) k++;\n    }\n    \n    // Calculate k! * (n-k)! % MOD\n    let res = 1n;\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    \n    return Number(res);\n}" }]} />

**Complexity**
- Time: O(n log log n) for the Sieve of Eratosthenes.
- Space: O(n) to store the boolean array of prime flags.
- Notes: This is the most efficient standard approach for finding primes up to a limit n.

## Iterative Primality Test

**Intuition**
Since the constraint n is very small (n &lt;= 100), we can iterate through every number from 1 to n and check if it is prime using a simple trial division method. This avoids the space complexity of the Sieve.

**Steps**
- Initialize a counter k = 0.
- Loop from 1 to n.
- For each number i, check if it is prime by testing divisibility from 2 up to the square root of i.
- If i is prime, increment k.
- Calculate k! * (n - k)! modulo 10⁹ + 7.

<CodeTabs client:load tabs={[{ name: "Python3", lang: "python", code: "class Solution:\n    def numPrimeArrangements(self, n: int) -&gt; int:\n        MOD = 10**9 + 7\n        \n        def is_prime(num):\n            if num &lt; 2:\n                return False\n            for i in range(2, int(num**0.5) + 1):\n                if num % i == 0:\n                    return False\n            return True\n        \n        k = 0\n        for i in range(1, n + 1):\n            if is_prime(i):\n                k += 1\n                \n        res = 1\n        for i in range(1, k + 1):\n            res = (res * i) % MOD\n        for i in range(1, n - k + 1):\n            res = (res * i) % MOD\n            \n        return res" },
{ name: "Java", lang: "java", code: "class Solution {\n    public int numPrimeArrangements(int n) {\n        int MOD = 1000000007;\n        \n        int k = 0;\n        for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n            if (isPrime(i)) {\n                k++;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        long res = 1;\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        \n        return (int) res;\n    }\n    \n    private boolean isPrime(int num) {\n        if (num &lt; 2) return false;\n        for (int i = 2; i * i &lt;= num; i++) {\n            if (num % i == 0) return false;\n        }\n        return true;\n    }\n}" },
{ name: "C++", lang: "cpp", code: "class Solution {\npublic:\n    int numPrimeArrangements(int n) {\n        const int MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n        \n        int k = 0;\n        for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; ++i) {\n            if (isPrime(i)) {\n                ++k;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        long long res = 1;\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= k; ++i) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        for (int i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; ++i) {\n            res = (res * i) % MOD;\n        }\n        \n        return (int)res;\n    }\n    \nprivate:\n    bool isPrime(int num) {\n        if (num &lt; 2) return false;\n        for (int i = 2; i * i &lt;= num; ++i) {\n            if (num % i == 0) return false;\n        }\n        return true;\n    }\n};" },
{ name: "JavaScript", lang: "javascript", code: "var numPrimeArrangements = function(n) {\n    const MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n    \n    const isPrime = (num) =&gt; {\n        if (num &lt; 2) return false;\n        for (let i = 2; i * i &lt;= num; i++) {\n            if (num % i === 0) return false;\n        }\n        return true;\n    };\n    \n    let k = 0;\n    for (let i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime(i)) k++;\n    }\n    \n    let res = 1n;\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    \n    return Number(res);\n};" },
{ name: "TypeScript", lang: "typescript", code: "function numPrimeArrangements(n: number): number {\n    const MOD = 1e9 + 7;\n    \n    const isPrime = (num: number): boolean =&gt; {\n        if (num &lt; 2) return false;\n        for (let i = 2; i * i &lt;= num; i++) {\n            if (num % i === 0) return false;\n        }\n        return true;\n    };\n    \n    let k = 0;\n    for (let i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) {\n        if (isPrime(i)) k++;\n    }\n    \n    let res = 1n;\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    for (let i = 2; i &lt;= n - k; i++) {\n        res = (res * BigInt(i)) % BigInt(MOD);\n    }\n    \n    return Number(res);\n}" }]} />

**Complexity**
- Time: O(n * sqrt(n)) because we check primality for each of the n numbers.
- Space: O(1) as we only use a few variables for counting and calculation.
- Notes: This is slower than the Sieve for large n, but perfectly acceptable and simpler for n &lt;= 100.

## Precomputation

**Intuition**
The constraints are extremely small (n &lt;= 100). We can precompute the answer for every possible n from 1 to 100 offline, store them in an array, and simply return the value at index n. This results in O(1) time complexity for the function call.

**Steps**
- Precompute an array `ans` where `ans[i]` holds the result for input i.
- In the solution function, simply return `ans[n]`.

<script is:inline type="application/ld+json">
{JSON.stringify({"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the time complexity of the Sieve of Eratosthenes approach?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The time complexity is O(n log log n) for finding the primes, plus O(n) for calculating the factorials."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why do we calculate factorials modulo 10⁹ + 7?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The number of valid permutations grows very quickly (factorial growth). Since the result must fit within standard integer limits and the problem specifies it, we return the result modulo 10⁹ + 7."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the space complexity of the Iterative Primality Test approach?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The space complexity is O(1) because we only use a few variables for counting and checking primality, without allocating an array of size n."}}]}).replace(/</g,'\u003c')}
